head: 77b58889
root_cause: L9 concurrency. The equivalence fixture pins T2PW_EXTRACTION_DRAWS=3 (strict and research cases). The 3 Stage-1 requests are byte-identical: one cassette key, 3 recorded answers served in the order requests ARRIVE. Sequential draws made request k draw k's by construction. Concurrent draws let a late-starting thread swap two answers; the merge keeps the first occurrence, so the merged Stage-1 payload changed, then Stage 2's prompt, and the cassette had no entry (ReplayMiss ask #1, 0 recorded). The research case (own child process, hash seed 0) flaked the same way (2 of the failing runs).
proof_of_cause: Forcing thread start order with a sleep in the draw thread (temporary, reverted): order [1,2,3] passes; [2,1,3] misses exactly key ad789a16...46c6 (the flaking key); [2,3,1], [1,3,2], [3,2,1] miss on 94287965, 3a23c147, 5b34ae11. Logs L9blogs/exp_*.log. Product impact nil (draws are exchangeable samples); it breaks replay and reproducibility.

On the base source 11 of 15 fail (the rest are N=1/no-op cases); log before2.log. The decisive before/after is the equivalence loop (5/15 vs 0/20) and the forced orders.
open_issues: A retry (request i>1) of draw k waits for request i of draw k-1 to be issued, or draw k-1 to end: if draw k-1 is still in a long first request, draw k's retry waits for it (bounded by the client's request timeouts). Only changes latency in retry cases; the spec asked for per-index ordering.

Request index counts provider attempts, so a 429 retry in one draw shifts its indices against another draw's; ordering is still acyclic and lock-free of deadlock, but exact pairing is only guaranteed when no draw has a transport-level retry (true in replay).
A fixture RECORDED with concurrent draws would store answers in completion order; the existing cassettes were recorded sequentially.
Replay: requests of the 3 draws are effectively issued one after another (each returns in ms); real runs overlap as before.
